solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Diamonds and hearts stored in memory by mouthing

indicators.note: a thing stored in a container sits inside it, so the card suit goes within the memory

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in a computer
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

indicators.note: mouthing a word means saying it, so we want a spelling that sounds like the clue word

parts.note: the little word by is said the same as the prefix bi-

explanation.surface: A card player memorises diamonds and hearts by reciting them aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds and hearts' reads as a pair of suits, but only hearts is wordplay; diamonds is the definition. 'mouthing' turns BY into BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of rhombus, the four-sided lozenge shape that a diamond on a playing card has.

clue.text: Physio for test series?

definitions.meaning: a masseur or physiotherapist who rubs the muscles
a set of matches, such as Test matches in cricket, played to decide a winner

explanation.definitionFit: One who rubs is a masseur; a best-of series of games in cricket or bridge is also called by this name.

clue.text: Writer wearing fancy flower shows hospitality to all comers

indicators.note: the writer wears the exclamation like a garment, so it goes round the writer

parts.note: 'Fancy!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'Oh!'
a pen is a writing instrument
a river is a flow-er; the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A writer in a flamboyant flower costume welcomes all visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword code for a river (something that flows), here the Ouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping an unrestricted welcome for any guest who calls is the idiom for this phrase.

clue.text: See 7
Unlawful politician joins guy, perhaps, in old tax office

indicators.note: the politician and the guy are placed in the tax office's abbreviation

parts.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority
MP is a Member of Parliament
a guy is a rope used to steady a tent, an example of a rope

explanation.surface: A politician teams up with some fellow inside the old tax office, which sounds dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' suggests a man; it is a guy rope. The Inland Revenue (IR) was the British tax office before 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not permitted by the rules or law is irregular, a near synonym of illicit.

clue.text: Controversial doctor to cut back

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

indicators.note: back tells us the little word is to be read in the reverse direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor makes contentious cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger doubts 'cut' adds anything; it seems to dress up 'back' as the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is one open to argument, debatable or disputed.

clue.text: One left spider weaving traps on counter

indicators.note: the shuffled letters close round the little word as a trap holds its catch
weaving makes a web, a mixing up, so the letters are rearranged
left means departed, so the letter for one goes from the creature's name

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lone spider, left behind, spins a web that catches things on a worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a kitchen worktop in the surface; it is the verb meaning reply. 'weaving' makes RESPD from what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter is to answer back or reply, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Make a phone-call precisely to turn somebody on?

definitions.meaning: on a keypad phone you dial by tapping keys exactly
the idiom for knowing just how to arouse or please a person

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal (assuming no dial phone); the second is the figurative idiom for stimulating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally keying in the correct digits, and figuratively doing exactly what excites or pleases someone.

clue.text: Humanitarians concerned about diabetic abandoned somewhere in Highlands

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: abandoned suggests emptied, so only the outside letters of the word stay

parts.note: Ross is a district of the Scottish Highlands, as in Ross and Cromarty

explanation.surface: Aid workers worried about a diabetic left stranded in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' empties 'diabetic' to D and C. Ross is part of the old Scottish county of Ross and Cromarty.
explanation.definitionFit: The international relief movement is a body of humanitarian aid workers.

clue.text: Managing the bar is a breeze

indicators.note: managing letters means handling and reorganising them, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Running the pub is easy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a breeze' looks like 'easy'; here it means a light puff of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A breath of wind is a slight breeze, a gentle stirring of air.

clue.text: Much beer consumed, admits old German lady

indicators.note: the word for consumed lets the others in, so they go inside it

parts.note: had, as in 'had dinner', means ate or consumed
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A lot of beer was drunk, an elderly German woman confesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cask holding about fifty-four gallons of ale, so a great quantity.

clue.text: Cake producer left unit, under pressure, in hands of Alfred?

indicators.note: held in the hands of the king, so the letters go inside his title

parts.note: Alfred the Great, the king who in legend burnt the cakes

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters for left and unit sit beneath the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
I stands for one, a unit

explanation.surface: A cake maker leaves the unit under pressure, in King Alfred's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: King Alfred famously burnt the cakes, a joke on the surface. Mr Kipling is a well-known British brand of cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Kipling is a famous British brand of packaged cakes, hence a maker of them.

clue.text: Country work accepted by two during crippling heat

indicators.note: the inner set of letters is placed within the shuffled word
crippling damages or twists something, so the letters are rearranged
the item accepted by the pair is taken in between them

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A country where work goes on in pairs during disabling heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crippling' shuffles the heat to ETHA, which is split around the pair holding the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in the Horn of Africa, with Addis Ababa as its capital.

clue.text: Ship's controlled by active person — not him

indicators.note: held by the active person, so the ship letters are kept inside that word

parts.note: a doer is someone who gets things done
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: The ship is commanded by an energetic person.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'not him' points back at the 'active person': the answer is the opposite, a lazy idler.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout or vagrant is the very opposite of a busy, energetic type.

clue.text: Son avoids breathing disorder during vacation in Beirut, bringing household linen

indicators.note: the shortened ailment goes within the emptied city name
vacation means emptying, so only the outer letters of the city remain
the son letter keeps away, so it is taken out

parts.note: asthma is a condition that makes breathing difficult

explanation.surface: A son escapes his asthma while on holiday in Beirut, taking some linen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' means emptying, not a holiday: Beirut leaves B and T. ASTHMA minus S is ATHMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A towelling mat for the bathroom floor, part of a home's textiles.

clue.text: Bond girl Laura's recreating in strip

indicators.note: the shuffled name is placed inside the word for strip

parts.note: to strip is to take your clothes off

indicators.note: recreating means making again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Laura is re-enacting something in a striptease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreating' makes RSULAA; the possessive S of Laura's counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss actress played Honey Ryder in Dr No, the first James Bond film.

clue.text: Pudding habit will be curbed by summer in France — famous last words!

indicators.note: being curbed by something means being held in by it, so these go inside

parts.note: été is French for summer
a pudding is a fat person, a tub
a rut is a fixed routine

explanation.surface: A habit of eating pudding will be restrained by summer in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pudding' suggests dessert but means a podgy person, a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar's dying reproach to his friend Brutus in Shakespeare is a celebrated final utterance.

clue.text: AWOL sailors on course, right away

parts.note: ABs are able seamen

indicators.note: away means gone, so the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: Sailors who were on a course have gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent without leave describes one who is missing from duty.

clue.text: Draining earth harmed herbaceous perennial

parts.note: bleeding a radiator or system means draining it

indicators.note: harmed means damaged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Draining the soil damaged a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicentra, a garden plant with heart-shaped pink flowers, returns each year.

clue.text: With a change of emphasis discussed, settle here around Chester

indicators.text: With a change of emphasis discussed
indicators.note: spoken aloud with the stress moved to the first syllable, the word sounds like a place

parts.note: to settle a matter is to decide it

explanation.surface: Talked over, with a change of emphasis, settle down here near Chester.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'decide' with stress on the first syllable. Deeside is the area along the River Dee by Chester.
explanation.definitionFit: The region along the River Dee near Chester carries this name.

clue.text: A doorman regularly tracks speed and pot

indicators.note: to track is to follow, so these letters come after the speed

parts.note: mph is miles per hour, a measure of speed

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A doorman routinely keeps an eye on speed and drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' suggests cannabis but is a jar. Every other letter of doorman gives ORA.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-handled ancient Greek or Roman jar for wine or oil.

clue.text: Charlie joins two hospital sections for the heart in US

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
ER is the emergency room

explanation.surface: Charlie links two hospital departments for an American heart clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: American spelling of the middle point or core of something.

clue.text: Missile one steers into area of golf course that's withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the assembled letters are read from the end
the steerer goes into the golf area

parts.note: a tee is where each hole begins
a cox steers a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A missile that one guides into part of a golf course is pulled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one steers' might suggest an ox; it is the cox of a rowing crew. TECOXE reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-made anti-ship guided rocket, famous from the Falklands War.

clue.text: Frank six deliveries inside for postmen

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled

indicators.note: inside points to the centre letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Six deliveries are put indoors for the postmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests post, but in cricket an over is six balls bowled. T is the middle of 'postmen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Open and unconcealed, as candid speech is plain and frank.

clue.text: Conspicuous light-coloured frames Picasso snubbed

indicators.note: the colour word frames the painter, holding him inside

parts.note: pale means light in colour

indicators.note: snubbed is read as cut short, so the last letter of the name goes

parts.note: Pablo was Picasso's first name

explanation.surface: A conspicuous pale picture frame ignores Picasso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' means docked here (snub-nosed): PABLO loses its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious enough to be noticed or felt, plainly evident.

clue.text: Footwear, amongst gardening equipment, dislodged spades

indicators.note: dislodged means shifted from its place, so the spades letter moves to the other end

parts.note: hoes are garden tools for weeding
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A shoe among the garden tools has knocked the spades over.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item of the outer covering worn on the foot.

clue.text: See 7
See copper closing brace to arrest destructive creature

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: a brace is a pair, so the closing two letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Watch a policeman close in to arrest a destructive creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman; it is the metal Cu. 'brace' means two, so take the last two letters of 'arrest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarming grasshopper that strips crops bare, a byword for devastation.

clue.text: Reputable bride meets everyone, holding back

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in reverse order
the three words hold the letters inside them across their junctions

explanation.surface: A respectable bride greets every guest while holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly regarded and respected, so having a good reputation.

clue.text: Calling nurse to clothe patient, third from the end

indicators.note: the carer clothes the letter, wrapping round it

parts.note: a carer looks after the sick, as a nurse does

indicators.note: count back three from the final letter of the word patient

explanation.surface: A nurse is called to dress the patient, third from the end of the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocation or profession is one's calling in life.
